Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheal dilation and extensive, progressive cystic bronchiectasis with multiple intrapulmonary cavities (especially evident in Figure 7 compared to Figure 1), which are hallmark features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). Management for this condition focuses on airway clearance and treating recurrent infections with antibiotics and physiotherapy.
